prompt: Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B that periodically reads moisture levels from a DFRobot Soil Moisture Sensor v2.0 (analog resistive) using an MCP3008 ADC connected on the SPI0 hardware bus, with CE0 on GPIO8 (BCM), MOSI on GPIO10 (BCM), MISO on GPIO9 (BCM), and SCLK on GPIO11 (BCM); the sensor’s analog output is wired to MCP3008 channel 0 (CH0), and the program must sample once per second, logging the raw 10‑bit ADC value (0‑1023) to the console together with a timestamp, while providing robust error handling for any SPI initialization or transfer failures, ensuring that the SPI handle is closed and the driver library is terminated cleanly on all exit paths, and supporting graceful shutdown when receiving SIGINT or SIGTERM.
raw:
```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <wiringPi.h>
#include <wiringPiSPI.h>

#define SPI_CHANNEL 0
#define SPI_SPEED 1000000
#define SPI_DELAY 0

#define ADC_CHANNEL 0
#define ADC_MAX_VALUE 1023

#define SLEEP_TIME 1

#define TIMESTAMP_FORMAT "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"

volatile sig_atomic_t running = 1;

void sigint_handler(int sig) {
    running = 0;
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    int spi_fd;
    int adc_value;
    time_t timestamp;
    struct tm *timestamp_tm;
    char timestamp_str[20];

    if (wiringPiSetup() == -1) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize wiringPi\n");
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    if (wiringPiSPISetup(SPI_CHANNEL, SPI_SPEED) == -1) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize SPI\n");
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    signal(SIGINT, sigint_handler);

    while (running) {
        spi_fd = wiringPiSPIDataRW(SPI_CHANNEL, NULL, 2);
        if (spi_fd == -1) {
            fprintf(stderr, "Failed to read SPI data: %s\n", strerror(errno));
            return EXIT_FAILURE;
        }

        adc_value = ((spi_fd & 0x0003) << 8) | (spi_fd >> 2);

        timestamp = time(NULL);
        timestamp_tm = localtime(&timestamp);
        strftime(timestamp_str, sizeof(timestamp_str), TIMESTAMP_FORMAT, timestamp_tm);

        printf("%s, %d\n", timestamp_str, adc_value);

        sleep(SLEEP_TIME);
    }

    return EXIT_SUCCESS;
}

prompt: Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 5 that continuously logs the sound level from a MAX9814 microphone amplifier and the ambient light level from a BH1750 sensor to a CSV file named tamper_log.csv, with each line containing a timestamp, sound_level_db, light_level_lux, and an error_code; the MAX9814 analog output must be read through an external MCP3008 ADC on SPI0 CE0 channel 0, the BH1750 must be accessed on I2C /dev/i2c‑1 with a 180 ms pause before reading its 2‑byte result, and the combined readings should be recorded every 5 seconds while any I2C communication errors or ADC read failures are captured as error codes alongside the sensor values, and the program must release the I2C file descriptor, the SPI file descriptor, and close the CSV file cleanly when receiving a SIGINT or SIGTERM.

prompt: Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B that continuously reads the DFROBOT Soil Moisture Sensor through an MCP3008 8‑channel 10‑bit ADC on SPI0 (CE0 on GPIO8, SCLK on GPIO11, MOSI on GPIO10, MISO on GPIO9, operating at 1 MHz, SPI mode 0) with the sensor connected to MCP3008 channel 0, samples the moisture value every 60 seconds, and activates a relay‑driven water pump on BCM GPIO18 (active high) whenever the reading falls below the threshold of 300 (out of 1023); each reading together with the pump status (ON or OFF) and a timestamp must be appended to a file named irrigation.log, and the program must verify successful initialization of all driver library APIs, opening of the SPI interface, and opening of the log file, handling any sensor read failures by logging an error and continuing; on receipt of SIGINT or SIGTERM the program must turn off the pump, close the SPI interface, close the log file, and cleanly terminate the driver library.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B that reads two potentiometers through an MCP3008 ADC on SPI channel 0 (1 MHz, mode 0) using MOSI on GPIO10, MISO on GPIO9, SCLK on GPIO11 and CE0 on GPIO8, maps each reading to a speed value, and drives two Adafruit Mini DC Motor with wires (Product ID 155) by PWM‑controlling Motor 1 enable on GPIO18 and Motor 2 enable on GPIO24 while setting direction with Motor 1 direction on GPIO23 and Motor 2 direction on GPIO25; the program must accelerate each motor from zero to the set speed, hold a constant‑speed phase of exactly 2 seconds, then decelerate back to zero, pause for 5 seconds, reverse the direction of both motors (Motor 1 forward and Motor 2 backward simultaneously or sequentially with a short delay as required), and repeat the cycle, while providing robust error handling for all driver and SPI operations and gracefully handling cases where a potentiometer is absent or the SPI bus reports an error, and must clean up all resources—including PWM, SPI, and GPIO—on normal exit or when receiving SIGINT or SIGTERM via appropriate signal handlers.

The source should include <stdint.h> for uint8_t and uint32_t types and must not use any external driver library for GPIO or SPI.

prompt: Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi that opens the USB camera on /dev/video0 in blocking mode (O_RDWR without O_NONBLOCK), queries the device capabilities to ensure both V4L2_CAP_VIDEO_CAPTURE and V4L2_CAP_STREAMING are present, sets the pixel format to V4L2_PIX_FMT_MJPEG with a width of 192 (the documented value) and V4L2_FIELD_NONE, requests four MMAP buffers, starts streaming, dequeues a single frame, verifies that the dequeued buffer’s bytesused field is greater than zero, and writes the raw MJPEG bytes directly to a file named image.jpg without any re‑encoding; every ioctl, open, mmap, and fopen call must have its return value checked and any failure reported with a descriptive perror/errno message, and a SIGINT/SIGTERM handler must be installed to stop streaming, unmap all buffers, free the buffer array, close the file and the device file descriptor on all exit paths, ensuring clean resource release.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi that controls a camera pan‑tilt mount using the board’s GPIO software PWM bus and four active‑low push‑buttons with internal pull‑ups, where the pan servo is connected to GPIO4 (BCM) and the tilt servo to GPIO5 (BCM), the tilt‑up button to GPIO6 (BCM), the tilt‑down button to GPIO7 (BCM), the pan‑left button to GPIO8 (BCM) and the pan‑right button to GPIO9 (BCM); the program must generate a 50 Hz PWM period (20 ms) with pulse widths ranging from 1 ms to 2 ms (corresponding to duty values of 50 to 100 out of 1000), initialize both servos to the mid‑position value 75, and on each button press adjust the corresponding axis by ±5 while clamping the position to the range 25–125, poll the button states every 50 ms, check the return status of every driver call and handle any request failures, and on receipt of SIGINT cleanly release all allocated resources.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi running Bookworm 64‑bit that opens the USB camera on /dev/video0, uses select() with a 2‑second timeout to wait for a frame, requests buffers, memory‑maps them, queues a buffer, starts streaming, dequeues the captured frame, stops streaming, unmaps the buffers, frees them and closes the file descriptor, handling SIGINT so that all these steps are performed cleanly on interruption; the captured image, originally in the documented YUYV format, must be converted to RGB24, processed with a blur filter, then encoded as a JPEG file named capture_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.jpg with quality set to 75, and every system call and memory allocation must be checked for failure with error messages printed to stderr and all resources released before exiting.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi that controls a camera pan‑tilt mount using two hobby servos driven over the GPIO hardware PWM bus, with four active‑low push‑buttons wired to ground and using the internal pull‑up resistors; the pan servo is connected to GPIO4 (BCM) and the tilt servo to GPIO5 (BCM), while the UP, DOWN, LEFT and RIGHT buttons are on GPIO6, GPIO7, GPIO8 and GPIO9 respectively, all using 50 Hz PWM where each loop iteration increments the pulse width by 10 µs and the loop delays 50 ms, the pulse widths must be clamped between 1000 µs (minimum) and 2000 µs (maximum) with a center position of 1500 µs, the program must initialize the driver library and check its return value, printing an error and exiting if initialization fails, output a startup message showing the pin assignments and the center position, respond to button presses by adjusting the appropriate servo pulse width in the allowed range, and install a SIGINT/SIGTERM handler that cleanly stops PWM on both servo pins using the library's API call, calls the library's API call() to release resources, and then exits.

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <pigpio.h>

#define PAN_SERVO_PIN 17
#define TILT_SERVO_PIN 18
#define PAN_SERVO_NEUTRAL 1500
#define TILT_SERVO_NEUTRAL 1500
#define PAN_SERVO_MIN 1000
#define PAN_SERVO_MAX 2000
#define TILT_SERVO_MIN 1000
#define TILT_SERVO_MAX 2000
#define SERVO_STEP 500
#define SERVO_FREQ 50
#define SERVO_RANGE 180
#define SERVO_DELAY 100

int pan_servo_pos = PAN_SERVO_NEUTRAL;
int tilt_servo_pos = TILT_SERVO_NEUTRAL;

void cleanup(int signum) {
    gpioServo(PAN_SERVO_PIN, PAN_SERVO_NEUTRAL);
    gpioServo(TILT_SERVO_PIN, TILT_SERVO_NEUTRAL);
    gpioTerminate();
    exit(0);
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    if (gpioInitialise() < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "pigpio initialisation failed: %s\n", strerror(errno));
        return 1;
    }

    gpioSetMode(PAN_SERVO_PIN, PI_OUTPUT);
    gpioSetMode(TILT_SERVO_PIN, PI_OUTPUT);
    gpioSetPWMfrequency(PAN_SERVO_PIN, SERVO_FREQ);
    gpioSetPWMfrequency(TILT_SERVO_PIN, SERVO_FREQ);
    gpioServo(PAN_SERVO_PIN, PAN_SERVO_NEUTRAL);
    gpioServo(TILT_SERVO_PIN, TILT_SERVO_NEUTRAL);

    signal(SIGINT, cleanup);

    char c;
    while (1) {
        c = getchar();
        if (c == 'q') {
            break;
        } else if (c == 'a') {
            pan_servo_pos -= SERVO_STEP;
            if (pan_servo_pos < PAN_SERVO_MIN) {
                fprintf(stderr, "Pan servo angle out of range: %d\n", pan_servo_pos);
                pan_servo_pos = PAN_SERVO_MIN;
            }
        } else if (c == 'd') {
            pan_servo_pos += SERVO_STEP;
            if (pan_servo_pos > PAN_SERVO_MAX) {
                fprintf(stderr, "Pan servo angle out of range: %d\n", pan_servo_pos);
                pan_servo_pos = PAN_SERVO_MAX;
            }
        } else if (c == 'w') {
            tilt_servo_pos -= SERVO_STEP;
            if (tilt_servo_pos < TILT_SERVO_MIN) {
                fprintf(stderr, "Tilt servo angle out of range: %d\n", tilt_servo_pos);
                tilt_servo_pos = TILT_SERVO_MIN;
            }
        } else if (c == 's') {
            tilt_servo_pos += SERVO_STEP;
            if (tilt_servo_pos > TILT_SERVO_MAX) {
                fprintf(stderr, "Tilt servo angle out of range: %d\n", tilt_servo_pos);
                tilt_servo_pos = TILT_SERVO_MAX;
            }
        } else {
            fprintf(stderr, "Invalid input: %c\n", c);
            continue;
        }

        if (gpioServo(PAN_SERVO_PIN, pan_servo_pos) < 0) {
            fprintf(stderr, "Failed to set pan servo position: %s\n", strerror(errno));
        }
        if (gpioServo(TILT_SERVO_PIN, tilt_servo_pos) < 0) {
            fprintf(stderr, "Failed to set tilt servo position: %s\n", strerror(errno));
        }

        gpioDelay(SERVO_DELAY);
    }

    cleanup(0);
    return 0;
}

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <pigpio.h>

#define BUZZER_PIN 18
#define SENSOR_PIN 17

FILE *fp;

void sig_handler(int signo)
{
    if (signo == SIGINT || signo == SIGTERM)
    {
        fprintf(fp, "Program terminated\n");
        fclose(fp);
        gpioTerminate();
        exit(0);
    }
}

int main(void)
{
    if (gpioInitialise() < 0)
    {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialise GPIO\n");
        return 1;
    }

    gpioSetMode(BUZZER_PIN, PI_OUTPUT);
    gpioSetMode(SENSOR_PIN, PI_INPUT);

    fp = fopen("obstacle_log.txt", "w");
    if (fp == NULL)
    {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to open log file\n");
        gpioTerminate();
        return 1;
    }

    signal(SIGINT, sig_handler);
    signal(SIGTERM, sig_handler);

    int prev_state = 0;
    int curr_state = 0;

    while (1)
    {
        curr_state = gpioRead(SENSOR_PIN);

        if (curr_state != prev_state)
        {
            time_t t = time(NULL);
            struct tm *tm = localtime(&t);
            char time_str[64];
            strftime(time_str, sizeof(time_str), "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z", tm);

            if (curr_state == 0)
            {
                fprintf(fp, "%s: Obstacle detected\n", time_str);
                gpioWrite(BUZZER_PIN, 1);
            }
            else
            {
                fprintf(fp, "%s: Obstacle removed\n", time_str);
                gpioWrite(BUZZER_PIN, 0);
            }

            prev_state = curr_state;
        }

        usleep(100000);
    }

    return 0;
}

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B that reads temperature and humidity from a Sensirion SHT35‑DIS‑B sensor on I2C bus 1 using the documented high‑repeatability, clock‑stretching‑disabled measurement command, validates the 8‑bit CRC for both the temperature and humidity words, and, after waiting at least 15 ms for the 6‑byte result, converts the raw values to degrees Celsius and percent relative humidity with the standard Sensirion formulas, then adds a sinusoidal offset of ±2 °C and ±5 % RH over a one‑hour period to simulate a greenhouse environment before logging each reading with an ISO‑8601 UTC timestamp to a file named “environmental_data.txt” every 5 seconds; if any I2C read/write or CRC check fails, the program must retry up to three times with a one‑second delay and, after exhausting retries, log NaN values, while also providing robust error handling for driver initialization, I2C open/read/write, and file open, and must handle SIGINT and SIGTERM to gracefully shut down by closing the I2C handle, flushing and closing the log file, and terminating the driver cleanly.

prompt: Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W that reads the temperature from an STLM75 digital temperature sensor on the I2C bus once per second, stores each reading in a 10‑element circular buffer in memory and computes a running average, then drives an LED connected to GPIO17 (BCM) so that the LED is turned on when the average temperature exceeds 28.0 °C and turned off otherwise; the program must verify that the driver library initializes correctly, that the I2C bus can be opened, and that each I2C read succeeds, skipping any iteration where a failure occurs, and it must handle SIGINT or SIGTERM by turning the LED off, closing the I2C handle and invoking the library’s cleanup call().

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B that reads CO₂, temperature and humidity from a Sensirion SCD30 CO₂ sensor on the I2C bus, samples the data every 5 seconds, and writes each sample to an air_quality.log file as a CSV line containing an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp followed by CO₂ in ppm, temperature in °C and humidity in %RH, flushing the log after each write; the program must implement ventilation control logic where CO₂ below 800 ppm results in an OFF state, between 800 ppm and 1199 ppm a LOW state, and 1200 ppm or above a HIGH state, and must robustly handle driver library initialization failures, I2C open/write/read errors, sensor non‑response, data‑not‑ready conditions and CRC mismatches by logging the error and continuing without crashing; a sigaction handler for SIGINT and SIGTERM must stop the periodic measurement, close the I2C handle, close the log file and invoke the library’s cleanup API call before exiting, and when the program is run in a mocked or emulated environment with no hardware it should log the lack of sensor access and exit gracefully with return code 0 rather than aborting.

```c
#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <gpiod.h>
#include <poll.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <sys/types.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include "scd30.h"

#define LOG_FILE "air_quality.log"
#define LOG_FILE_MODE (S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR | S_IRGRP | S_IROTH)
#define LOG_FILE_PERMS (S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR | S_IRGRP | S_IWGRP | S_IROTH | S_IWOTH)
#define LOG_FILE_MAX_SIZE (1024 * 1024)
#define LOG_FILE_MAX_LINES 10000

#define SCD30_I2C_BUS 1
#define SCD30_I2C_ADDR 0x61

#define SCD30_MEASUREMENT_INTERVAL_S 5

#define VENTILATION_CO2_LOW 800
#define VENTILATION_CO2_HIGH 1200

#define VENTILATION_GPIO_CHIP "gpiochip0"
#define VENTILATION_GPIO_LINE 17

#define VENTILATION_STATE_OFF 0
#define VENTILATION_STATE_LOW 1
#define VENTILATION_STATE_HIGH 2

#define VENTILATION_STATE_STR_OFF "OFF"
#define VENTILATION_STATE_STR_LOW "LOW"
#define VENTILATION_STATE_STR_HIGH "HIGH"

static volatile sig_atomic_t running = 1;

static int log_fd = -1;
static struct gpiod_line *ventilation_gpio_line = NULL;
static struct scd30_dev *scd30 = NULL;

static void sig_handler(int sig) {
    running = 0;
}

static void cleanup(void) {
    if (scd30 != NULL) {
        scd30_close(scd30);
        scd30 = NULL;
    }
    if (ventilation_gpio_line != NULL) {
        gpiod_line_release(ventilation_gpio_line);
        ventilation_gpio_line = NULL;
    }
    if (log_fd != -1) {
        close(log_fd);
        log_fd = -1;
    }
}

static int init_log(void) {
    struct stat st;
    int ret;

    ret = stat(LOG_FILE, &st);
    if (ret == -1) {
        if (errno != ENOENT) {
            perror("stat");
            return -1;
        }
    } else {
        if (st.st_size >= LOG_FILE_MAX_SIZE) {
            fprintf(stderr, "log file size exceeds maximum\n");
            return -1;
        }
        if (st.st_size > 0) {
            FILE *fp = fopen(LOG_FILE, "r");
            if (fp == NULL) {
                perror("fopen");
                return -1;
            }
            int line_count = 0;
            char line[1024];
            while (fgets(line, sizeof(line), fp) != NULL) {
                line_count++;
            }
            fclose(fp);
            if (line_count >= LOG_FILE_MAX_LINES) {
                fprintf(stderr, "log file line count exceeds maximum\n");
                return -1;
            }
        }
    }

    log_fd = open(LOG_FILE, O_WRONLY | O_APPEND | O_CREAT, LOG_FILE_PERMS);
    if (log_fd == -1) {
        perror("open");
        return -1;
    }

    return 0;
}

static int init_scd30(void) {
    scd30 = scd30_open(SCD30_I2C_BUS, SCD30_I2C_ADDR);
    if (scd30 == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "failed to open SCD30\n");
        return -1;
    }

    if (scd30_set_measurement_interval(scd30, SCD30_MEASUREMENT_INTERVAL_S) != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "failed to set measurement interval\n");
        return -1;
    }

    if (scd30_start_periodic_measurement(scd30) != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "failed to start periodic measurement\n");
        return -1;
    }

    return 0;
}

static int init_ventilation(void) {
    struct gpiod_chip *chip = gpiod_chip_open_by_name(VENTILATION_GPIO_CHIP);
    if (chip == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "failed to open GPIO chip\n");
        return -1;
    }

    ventilation_gpio_line = gpiod_chip_get_line(chip, VENTILATION_GPIO_LINE);
    if (ventilation_gpio_line == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "failed to get GPIO line\n");
        return -1;
    }

    if (gpiod_line_request_output(ventilation_gpio_line, "ventilation", 0) != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "failed to request GPIO line\n");
        return -1;
    }

    return 0;
}

static int set_ventilation_state(int state) {
    if (gpiod_line_set_value(ventilation_gpio_line, state) != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "failed to set GPIO line value\n");
        return -1;
    }

    return 0;
}

static int log_air_quality(struct scd30_measurement *measurement) {
    char buf[1024];
    struct tm tm;
    time_t t = time(NULL);
    if (t == -1) {
        perror("time");
        return -1;
    }
    if (localtime_r(&t, &tm) == NULL) {
        perror("localtime_r");
        return -1;
    }
    if (strftime(buf, sizeof(buf), "%FT%TZ", &tm) == 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "strftime failed\n");
        return -1;
    }
    int ret = dprintf(log_fd, "%s,%d,%d,%d\n", buf, measurement->co2, measurement->temperature, measurement->humidity);
    if (ret < 0) {
        perror("dprintf");
        return -1;
    }
    if (fsync(log_fd) != 0) {
        perror("fsync");
        return -1;
    }

    return 0;
}

static int set_ventilation_state_from_co2(int co2) {
    if (co2 < VENTILATION_CO2_LOW) {
        return set_ventilation_state(VENTILATION_STATE_OFF);
    } else if (co2 < VENTILATION_CO2_HIGH) {
        return set_ventilation_state(VENTILATION_STATE_LOW);
    } else {
        return set_ventilation_state(VENTILATION_STATE_HIGH);
    }
}

static int get_ventilation_state_str(char *buf, size_t size) {
    int ret = gpiod_line_get_value(ventilation_gpio_line);
    if (ret == -1) {
        fprintf(stderr, "failed to get GPIO line value\n");
        return -1;
    }
    switch (ret) {
    case VENTILATION_STATE_OFF:
        return snprintf(buf, size, VENTILATION_STATE_STR_OFF);
    case VENTILATION_STATE_LOW:
        return snprintf(buf, size, VENTILATION_STATE_STR_LOW);
    case VENTILATION_STATE_HIGH:
        return snprintf(buf, size, VENTILATION_STATE_STR_HIGH);
    default:
        fprintf(stderr, "invalid GPIO line value\n");
        return -1;
    }
}

static int get_co2_str(char *buf, size_t size, int co2) {
    if (co2 < 0) {
        return snprintf(buf, size, "N/A");
    } else {
        return snprintf(buf, size, "%d", co2);
    }
}

static int get_temperature_str(char *buf, size_t size, int temperature) {
    if (temperature < 0) {
        return snprintf(buf, size, "N/A");
    } else {
        return snprintf(buf, size, "%d.%02d", temperature / 100, temperature % 100);
    }
}

static int get_humidity_str(char *buf, size_t size, int humidity) {
    if (humidity < 0) {
        return snprintf(buf, size, "N/A");
    } else {
        return snprintf(buf, size, "%d.%02d", humidity / 100, humidity % 100);
    }
}

static int print_air_quality(struct scd30_measurement *measurement) {
    char ventilation_state_str[16];
    char co2_str[16];
    char temperature_str[16];
    char humidity_str[16];
    if (get_ventilation_state_str(ventilation_state_str, sizeof(ventilation_state_str)) == -1) {
        return -1;
    }
    if (get_co2_str(co2_str, sizeof(co2_str), measurement->co2) == -1) {
        return -1;
    }
    if (get_temperature_str(temperature_str, sizeof(temperature_str), measurement->temperature) == -1) {
        return -1;
    }
    if (get_humidity_str(humidity_str, sizeof(humidity_str), measurement->humidity) == -1) {
        return -1;
    }
    printf("Ventilation: %s\n", ventilation_state_str);
    printf("CO₂: %s ppm\n", co2_str);
    printf("Temperature: %s °C\n", temperature_str);
    printf("Humidity: %s %%RH\n", humidity_str);

    return 0;
}

int main(void) {
    struct scd30_measurement measurement;
    struct pollfd pfd;
    int ret;

    if (init_log() != 0) {
        goto error;
    }

    if (init_scd30() != 0) {
        goto error;
    }

    if (init_ventilation() != 0) {
        goto error;
    }

    if (set_ventilation_state_from_co2(-1) != 0) {
        goto error;
    }

    if (print_air_quality(&measurement) != 0) {
        goto error;
    }

    pfd.fd = scd30_get_fd(scd30);
    pfd.events = POLLIN;

    struct sigaction sa;
    memset(&sa, 0, sizeof(sa));
    sa.sa_handler = sig_handler;
    if (sigaction(SIGINT, &sa, NULL) != 0) {
        perror("sigaction");
        goto error;
    }
    if (sigaction(SIGTERM, &sa, NULL) != 0) {
        perror("sigaction");
        goto error;
    }

    while (running) {
        ret = poll(&pfd, 1, -1);
        if (ret == -1) {
            if (errno == EINTR) {
                continue;
            }
            perror("poll");
            goto error;
        }
        if (ret == 0) {
            continue;
        }
        if (pfd.revents & POLLIN) {
            ret = scd30_read_measurement(scd30, &measurement);
            if (ret == -1) {
                if (errno == EAGAIN) {
                    continue;
                }
                perror("scd30_read_measurement");
                goto error;
            }
            if (ret == 0) {
                continue;
            }
            if (log_air_quality(&measurement) != 0) {
                goto error;
            }
            if (print_air_quality(&measurement) != 0) {
                goto error;
            }
            if (set_ventilation_state_from_co2(measurement.co2) != 0) {
                goto error;
            }
        }
    }

    cleanup();
    return 0;

error:
    cleanup();
    return 1;
}

prompt: Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W that bit‑bangs a single‑wire DHT11 temperature/humidity sensor on GPIO4 (BCM, physical pin 7) using the provided API call for microsecond timing, the provided API call for GPIO direction control, the provided API call for reading and writing pin levels, and the provided API call for clean shutdown; the program must generate the start signal by pulling the line low for at least 18 ms, then releasing it so the sensor can respond with an 80 µs low pulse followed by an 80 µs high pulse, after which each of the 40 data bits is transmitted beginning with a 50 µs low period and a high period of about 26‑28 µs for a ‘0’ or about 70 µs for a ‘1’, sampling the sensor no more often than every 2 seconds (the DHT11 minimum interval is 1 s), decode the 40 bits into humidity integer (byte 0), humidity decimal (byte 1, always 0), temperature integer (byte 2), temperature decimal (byte 3, always 0) and verify the checksum, write each successful reading to a file named dht11_readings.txt with an ISO‑8601 timestamp, detect and log timeouts on the start signal, response, and each data bit as well as checksum failures and sensor‑absent conditions such as a line stuck high or low, recording each error with a timestamp and a status code, and on receipt of SIGINT or SIGTERM release the GPIO resources via the library’s cleanup API, close any open file handles, and exit gracefully.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W that reads temperature and humidity from an Adafruit SHT31-D sensor on the I2C bus using SDA on GPIO2 (BCM, bus 1) and SCL on GPIO3 (BCM, bus 1), waiting at least 15 ms after issuing the measurement command and logging a new reading every 5 seconds to a file named sht31d_data.log with ISO‑8601 timestamps in the format “YYYY‑MM‑DD HH:MM:SS,temperature,humidity”, while checking that the driver library initializes correctly, that the I2C interface opens, that the log file opens, and that each I2C write, I2C read and CRC‑8 validation (using the documented polynomial and initial value) succeed, retrying any failed I2C transaction up to three times and, if the sensor continues to fail, logging the error with a timestamp and continuing operation, and finally handling SIGINT or SIGTERM by closing the I2C handle, closing the log file, and terminating the driver library; the program must read exactly six bytes per measurement (two bytes temperature plus one CRC, two bytes humidity plus one CRC) and validate each CRC‑8 as specified.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W that continuously reads the temperature from a Sensirion STS40 I2C temperature sensor on the I2C bus, waiting 10 ms after each trigger for the conversion to complete and sampling the value every 5 seconds, logging each reading together with an ISO‑8601 timestamp to a file named temperature_log.txt; the program must open the I2C device with open(), set the slave address using ioctl(I2C_SLAVE), read exactly three bytes (two data bytes and one CRC8 byte), verify the CRC8 using the Sensirion‑specified polynomial, and on any error condition—including failures to open the device, ioctl, read, write, CRC mismatch, or open the log file—print a descriptive message to stderr and then continue looping; it must also install handlers for SIGINT and SIGTERM that cleanly close the I2C file descriptor and the log file before exiting, and run indefinitely in an infinite loop.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W that continuously monitors air‑duct pressure in a simulated HVAC system using the Sensirion SDP810‑500Pa differential pressure sensor on the I2C bus, triggering a measurement, waiting at least 50 ms, then reading the 9‑byte result (2 bytes pressure, 1 byte CRC, 2 bytes temperature, 1 byte CRC, 3 bytes scale factor) once per second, validating every I2C read and write as well as each CRC‑8 using the polynomial and initial value documented for the sensor, logging each successful sample to a file named hvac_pressure_log.txt in CSV format with columns timestamp, pressure_Pa, temperature_C, and on any I2C or CRC error writing an error line with the timestamp and continuing, checking the return of every initialization call (the two required library API calls and fopen) and exiting with an error message if any fails, and handling SIGINT (Ctrl+C) by closing the I2C handle, flushing and closing the log file, and calling the library’s cleanup API function before terminating.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B that continuously reads the Sensirion SHT40 sensor on I2C bus 1, issuing the measurement command, waiting at least 10 ms, then reading exactly six bytes, and streams the live temperature and humidity values to a local HTTP server on port 8080 using the library’s API call to serve an HTML page that displays the current temperature and humidity while clamping humidity to the range 0‑100 %; the implementation must include robust error handling for I2C communication such as sensor absence or bus errors with up to three retries per read, and must cleanly release all resources on every exit path, handling SIGINT and SIGTERM signals appropriately.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B that reads temperature from a Texas Instruments TMP102 on I2C bus 1 using the documented address, performs a measurement every 5 seconds, and appends each result to a timestamped CSV file named temperature_log.csv with lines formatted as “YYYY‑MM‑DD HH:MM:SS,XX.XX”; the program must include standard headers such as errno.h and stdint.h to compile without warnings, check the success of all initialization and I/O calls, log any read failure to stderr while skipping that entry, and install a SIGINT handler so that when Ctrl+C is pressed the I2C handle is closed, the driver library is terminated, and the program exits cleanly.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W that continuously reads temperature and humidity from a Texas Instruments HDC2010 sensor on I2C bus 1 using the documented address, polling the sensor’s MEASUREMENT_CONFIG register until bit 0 clears or a timeout of roughly 500 ms occurs, then outputs the readings to the console every five seconds; the implementation must check the result of every driver call, detect a missing sensor (NAK) and any bus‑error conditions, retry transient I2C failures only up to a defined maximum count, and include a clean shutdown triggered by Ctrl +C via a signal handler that sets a volatile sig_atomic_t flag, closes the I2C handle, and invokes the library’s API call() before exiting.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 4 Model B that samples a BMP180 pressure sensor on I2C bus 1 using the documented address, employing the library's API call for I2C communication and the library's API call for a hardware timer that triggers every 50 ms; each reading must be stored in a circular buffer sized to hold timestamped pressure values for the last 60 seconds, from which a rolling average is computed, and if the current pressure deviates by more than 5 hPa from that average the program shall assert an active‑HIGH alert on GPIO24, logging the alert to stderr, while also logging any I2C failures or sensor absence with robust error handling; the sampling loop must use the library's API call for the 50 ms timer, and on receipt of SIGINT the program must cleanly release resources by closing the I2C interface, resetting GPIO24, and terminating the driver library.

Write a C program for the Raspberry Pi 5 that actively manages the official Raspberry Pi 5 Active Cooler by reading the CPU temperature from /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone0/temp and the current fan state from /sys/class/thermal/cooling_device0/cur_state, polling the temperature every 5 seconds, applying a tiered speed map where temperatures below 45 °C set the fan state to 0 (off), below 55 °C set state 1, below 65 °C set state 2, and 65 °C or higher set state 3 (maximum), first validating the cooling device’s max_state before any write, and writing the new state back to the same cooling_device sysfs entry only when the speed changes; each fan speed change must be logged with a timestamp to /var/log/fan_control.log, all file opens, reads, writes, and parses must be checked for errors with transient read failures simply causing the program to retry on the next cycle, and the program must handle graceful shutdown on SIGINT or SIGTERM by setting the fan to state 0, logging the shutdown event, and exiting cleanly.

prompt: Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ that continuously polls a KY-033 Obstacle Avoidance Sensor Module connected on the GPIO bus, using the sensor output on GPIO4 (BCM pin 7) configured as an input with the internal pull‑up resistor enabled, sampling every 50 ms; the program must initialize the driver library and verify success, printing an error to stderr and returning a non‑zero code if initialization fails, record each detection (the sensor drives the line LOW when an obstacle is within the threshold and HIGH otherwise) in a circular buffer of 100 entries overwriting the oldest when full, emit an alert to stdout on every detection, and on receipt of SIGINT release all driver resources, then dump the entire buffer in chronological order to stdout with human‑readable timestamps before exiting cleanly, while ensuring no deprecated APIs are used.
raw:
```
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <pigpio.h>

#define BUFFER_SIZE 100
#define SENSOR_PIN 4
#define SENSOR_POLL_INTERVAL 50

typedef struct {
    int value;
    time_t timestamp;
} BufferEntry;

BufferEntry buffer[BUFFER_SIZE];
int bufferIndex = 0;

void handleSignal(int signal) {
    // Release resources
    gpioTerminate();

    // Dump buffer
    for (int i = 0; i < BUFFER_SIZE; i++) {
        int index = (bufferIndex + i) % BUFFER_SIZE;
        BufferEntry entry = buffer[index];
        printf("%ld: %d\n", entry.timestamp, entry.value);
    }

    exit(0);
}

int main() {
    // Initialize driver library
    if (gpioInitialise() < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize driver library\n");
        return 1;
    }

    // Set up signal handler
    signal(SIGINT, handleSignal);

    // Set up sensor pin
    if (gpioSetMode(SENSOR_PIN, PI_INPUT) != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to set sensor pin mode\n");
        return 1;
    }
    if (gpioSetPullUpDown(SENSOR_PIN, PI_PUD_UP) != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to set sensor pin pull-up\n");
        return 1;
    }

    // Start polling sensor
    gpioSetAlertFunc(SENSOR_PIN, NULL);
    gpioSetAlertFuncEx(SENSOR_PIN, NULL);
    gpioSetAlertFuncEx(SENSOR_PIN, [](int gpio, int level, uint32_t tick) {
        // Record detection in buffer
        BufferEntry entry = {level, time(NULL)};
        buffer[bufferIndex] = entry;
        bufferIndex = (bufferIndex + 1) % BUFFER_SIZE;

        // Print alert
        printf("Alert: Obstacle detected at %ld\n", entry.timestamp);
    });

    // Poll sensor
    while (1) {
        gpioRead(SENSOR_PIN);
        time_sleep(SENSOR_POLL_INTERVAL / 1000.0);
    }

    return 0;
}

prompt: Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ that continuously polls three KY-033 Obstacle Avoidance Sensors (IR reflective, digital output) connected via the GPIO bus, with the left sensor on GPIO17 (BCM), the middle sensor on GPIO27 (BCM) and the right sensor on GPIO22 (BCM), sampling each sensor every 50 ms and writing each timestamped reading to a CSV file named path_log.csv using ISO‑8601 timestamps and columns “timestamp,left,middle,right” where each sensor value is recorded as 0 or 1; the program must verify that the library’s API call to open the GPIO chip succeeds, that each line can be requested as an input, and that all file I/O operations succeed, must include system headers such as <errno.h> and <stdbool.h> so it compiles without warnings under gcc ‑Wall ‑Wextra, and must handle a SIGINT signal by cleanly releasing all GPIO lines, closing the chip, flushing and closing the log file before exiting.

#include <errno.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <sys/stat.h>
#include <sys/types.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#include <pigpio.h>

#define LOG_FILE "path_log.csv"
#define LOG_HEADER "timestamp,left,middle,right\n"

#define GPIO_CHIP "gpiochip0"
#define GPIO_LEFT 17
#define GPIO_MIDDLE 27
#define GPIO_RIGHT 22

#define SENSOR_POLL_MS 50

static int log_fd = -1;
static int gpio_chip = -1;
static int gpio_left = -1;
static int gpio_middle = -1;
static int gpio_right = -1;

static void cleanup(void)
{
    if (gpio_left != -1) {
        gpioSetMode(gpio_left, PI_INPUT);
        gpio_left = -1;
    }
    if (gpio_middle != -1) {
        gpioSetMode(gpio_middle, PI_INPUT);
        gpio_middle = -1;
    }
    if (gpio_right != -1) {
        gpioSetMode(gpio_right, PI_INPUT);
        gpio_right = -1;
    }
    if (gpio_chip != -1) {
        gpioTerminate();
        gpio_chip = -1;
    }
    if (log_fd != -1) {
        close(log_fd);
        log_fd = -1;
    }
}

static void sigint_handler(int signum)
{
    cleanup();
    exit(EXIT_SUCCESS);
}

static void log_sensor_readings(void)
{
    struct timespec ts;
    char buf[1024];
    int left, middle, right;

    if (clock_gettime(CLOCK_REALTIME, &ts) != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "clock_gettime: %s\n", strerror(errno));
        return;
    }
    if (gpioRead(gpio_left, &left) != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "gpioRead(left): %s\n", strerror(errno));
        return;
    }
    if (gpioRead(gpio_middle, &middle) != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "gpioRead(middle): %s\n", strerror(errno));
        return;
    }
    if (gpioRead(gpio_right, &right) != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "gpioRead(right): %s\n", strerror(errno));
        return;
    }
    if (strftime(buf, sizeof(buf), "%FT%T%z", gmtime(&ts.tv_sec)) == 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "strftime: %s\n", strerror(errno));
        return;
    }
    if (snprintf(buf + strlen(buf), sizeof(buf) - strlen(buf), ",%d,%d,%d\n", left, middle, right) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "snprintf: %s\n", strerror(errno));
        return;
    }
    if (write(log_fd, buf, strlen(buf)) != strlen(buf)) {
        fprintf(stderr, "write: %s\n", strerror(errno));
        return;
    }
}

int main(void)
{
    struct sigaction sa;

    if (gpioInitialise() < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "gpioInitialise: %s\n", gpioGetErrorText(gpioGetLastError()));
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    gpio_chip = gpioOpen(GPIO_CHIP);
    if (gpio_chip < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "gpioOpen: %s\n", gpioGetErrorText(gpioGetLastError()));
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    gpio_left = gpioSetMode(GPIO_LEFT, PI_INPUT);
    if (gpio_left < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "gpioSetMode(left): %s\n", gpioGetErrorText(gpioGetLastError()));
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    gpio_middle = gpioSetMode(GPIO_MIDDLE, PI_INPUT);
    if (gpio_middle < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "gpioSetMode(middle): %s\n", gpioGetErrorText(gpioGetLastError()));
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    gpio_right = gpioSetMode(GPIO_RIGHT, PI_INPUT);
    if (gpio_right < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "gpioSetMode(right): %s\n", gpioGetErrorText(gpioGetLastError()));
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    log_fd = open(LOG_FILE, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, S_IRUSR | S_IWUSR);
    if (log_fd < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "open: %s\n", strerror(errno));
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    if (write(log_fd, LOG_HEADER, strlen(LOG_HEADER)) != strlen(LOG_HEADER)) {
        fprintf(stderr, "write: %s\n", strerror(errno));
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    memset(&sa, 0, sizeof(sa));
    sa.sa_handler = sigint_handler;
    if (sigaction(SIGINT, &sa, NULL) != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "sigaction: %s\n", strerror(errno));
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }
    for (;;) {
        log_sensor_readings();
        gpioDelay(SENSOR_POLL_MS * 1000);
    }
    return EXIT_SUCCESS;
}

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 5 that polls four Keywish KY-033 4‑Way Infrared Tracking Module sensors connected via GPIO—sensor 1 on GPIO17 (BCM), sensor 2 on GPIO18 (BCM), sensor 3 on GPIO27 (BCM), and sensor 4 on GPIO22 (BCM)—every 100 ms, reading each active‑low output (0 indicates line or obstacle detected, 1 indicates no line), and appends a row to a timestamped CSV file named tracking_log.csv with columns timestamp,sensor1,sensor2,sensor3,sensor4, writing a header row if the file does not yet exist; the program must robustly check every initialization and read call, printing clear error messages to stderr and continuing when possible if a GPIO request or read fails, must use the modern driver library API calls for GPIO handling, and must handle SIGINT and SIGTERM to perform a graceful shutdown that releases all driver resources, closes and flushes the CSV file after each write to prevent data loss on abrupt termination.

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <pigpio.h>

#define SENSOR_1 17
#define SENSOR_2 18
#define SENSOR_3 27
#define SENSOR_4 22
#define POLL_INTERVAL 100
#define CSV_FILE "tracking_log.csv"

FILE *csv_file;

void sig_handler(int signo)
{
    if (signo == SIGINT || signo == SIGTERM) {
        printf("Received signal %d, shutting down...\n", signo);
        fclose(csv_file);
        gpioTerminate();
        exit(0);
    }
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
    int sensor_values[4];
    char csv_line[100];
    time_t current_time;
    struct tm *time_info;

    if (gpioInitialise() < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize GPIO\n");
        return 1;
    }

    gpioSetMode(SENSOR_1, PI_INPUT);
    gpioSetMode(SENSOR_2, PI_INPUT);
    gpioSetMode(SENSOR_3, PI_INPUT);
    gpioSetMode(SENSOR_4, PI_INPUT);

    csv_file = fopen(CSV_FILE, "a");
    if (csv_file == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to open CSV file: %s\n", strerror(errno));
        gpioTerminate();
        return 1;
    }

    signal(SIGINT, sig_handler);
    signal(SIGTERM, sig_handler);

    while (1) {
        sensor_values[0] = gpioRead(SENSOR_1);
        sensor_values[1] = gpioRead(SENSOR_2);
        sensor_values[2] = gpioRead(SENSOR_3);
        sensor_values[3] = gpioRead(SENSOR_4);

        current_time = time(NULL);
        time_info = localtime(&current_time);
        strftime(csv_line, sizeof(csv_line), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", time_info);
        fprintf(csv_file, "%s,%d,%d,%d,%d\n", csv_line, sensor_values[0], sensor_values[1], sensor_values[2], sensor_values[3]);
        fflush(csv_file);

        gpioDelay(POLL_INTERVAL * 1000);
    }

    return 0;
}

The program uses gpioDelay to pause for the specified interval between reads.

The program uses gpioTerminate to release all GPIO resources when it receives a signal.

The program uses fflush to ensure that the data is written to the CSV file immediately after each write.

prompt: Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W that continuously polls an Adafruit LSM303DLHC accelerometer on I2C bus 1 at 10 Hz, computes the total G‑force magnitude, and when that magnitude exceeds a configurable threshold (default 2.0 G, settable with a ‑t command‑line argument) triggers an impact interrupt by setting GPIO17 (BCM numbering) as an output and pulsing it HIGH for 50 ms, while also logging the timestamped accelerometer data to a file named impact_log.txt; the program must check the result of every I2C read and write operation, handle cases where the sensor is absent or the bus reports errors, and ensure that on any exit path—including receipt of SIGINT or SIGTERM—it cleanly releases all resources such as the I2C handle, the GPIO pin, and any driver state.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W that reads ambient light and color data from an Analog Devices ADPD188BI optical sensor on I2C bus 1, samples the sensor every 500 ms, combines the ALS LSB and MSB into a 16‑bit unsigned value, and logs each timestamped reading of ALS, red, green and blue channels to a CSV file named color_log.csv with a header row; the program must also control an LED connected to GPIO18 (BCM) using hardware PWM so that brighter ambient light increases the LED brightness, handle any I2C errors such as failed writes, reads or a missing sensor by writing an error message to stderr and retrying after a 100 ms delay, and implement signal handling for SIGINT and SIGTERM to perform a graceful shutdown that closes the I2C handle, turns off the LED and closes the CSV file.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi Zero W that continuously reads the Adafruit FXOS8700CQ 6‑Axis Accelerometer/Magnetometer over I2C bus 1 at a 50 ms interval, first verifying the WHO_AM_I identifier on startup and aborting with a clear error message if it does not match, then placing the device in standby, configuring the sensor for a ±2 g range, and finally activating it for a 200 Hz output data rate; each loop must compute the acceleration magnitude from the three axes, and whenever the magnitude exceeds a defined impact threshold the program should append a line to “impact_log.txt” containing the current timestamp and the raw x, y, z values and the computed magnitude formatted as “YYYY‑MM‑DD HH:MM:SS,x,y,z,magnitude” with three decimal places, while checking the return value of every I2C call, printing a diagnostic to stderr on read errors and continuing the loop rather than crashing, and the application must handle SIGINT (Ctrl‑C) by gracefully closing the I2C handle, invoking the appropriate library shutdown call, and exiting cleanly.

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <pigpio.h>

#define PIR_PIN 4
#define LED_PIN 17
#define POLLING_INTERVAL 100
#define ACTIVATION_DURATION 60

FILE *log_file;

void sig_handler(int signo)
{
    if (signo == SIGINT || signo == SIGTERM) {
        gpioWrite(LED_PIN, 0);
        gpioTerminate();
        fclose(log_file);
        exit(0);
    }
}

int main(void)
{
    if (gpioInitialise() < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize GPIO library\n");
        return 1;
    }

    gpioSetMode(PIR_PIN, PI_INPUT);
    gpioSetMode(LED_PIN, PI_OUTPUT);

    log_file = fopen("security_log.txt", "a");
    if (log_file == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to open log file\n");
        gpioTerminate();
        return 1;
    }

    signal(SIGINT, sig_handler);
    signal(SIGTERM, sig_handler);

    time_t start_time, end_time;
    int pir_state = 0;

    while (1) {
        int current_state = gpioRead(PIR_PIN);

        if (current_state != pir_state) {
            if (current_state == 1) {
                time(&start_time);
                gpioWrite(LED_PIN, 1);
                fprintf(log_file, "%s: LED activated\n", ctime(&start_time));
            } else {
                time(&end_time);
                gpioWrite(LED_PIN, 0);
                fprintf(log_file, "%s: LED deactivated (duration: %ld seconds)\n", ctime(&end_time), end_time - start_time);
            }
            fflush(log_file);
            pir_state = current_state;
        }

        usleep(POLLING_INTERVAL * 1000);
    }

    return 0;
}

The program opens the log file in append mode and writes the activation and deactivation events to the file. The program also handles the SIGINT and SIGTERM signals to cleanly terminate the program and turn off the LED.

### Note:
The program assumes that the PIR sensor is connected to GPIO 4 and the LED is connected to GPIO 17. The program also assumes that the pigpio library is installed and configured correctly on the Raspberry Pi.

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <pigpio.h>

#define PIR_PIN 17
#define RELAY_PIN 18
#define LOG_FILE "door_events.log"
#define RATE_LIMIT 2000

FILE *log_file;
int pir_state = 0;
int relay_state = 0;
time_t last_event_time = 0;

void handle_pir_event(int pin, int level, uint32_t tick) {
    if (level == 1 && pir_state == 0) {
        // Motion detected
        pir_state = 1;
        time_t current_time = time(NULL);
        if (current_time - last_event_time >= RATE_LIMIT / 1000) {
            // Rate limit not exceeded
            last_event_time = current_time;
            fprintf(log_file, "%ld Motion detected\n", current_time);
            fflush(log_file);
            gpioWrite(RELAY_PIN, 1);
            relay_state = 1;
            gpioSetTimerFunc(500, 1, NULL);
        }
    }
}

void handle_relay_event(void) {
    gpioWrite(RELAY_PIN, 0);
    relay_state = 0;
    fprintf(log_file, "%ld Door unlocked\n", time(NULL));
    fflush(log_file);
}

void handle_signal(int signum) {
    if (signum == SIGINT) {
        // Handle SIGINT signal
        gpioTerminate();
        fclose(log_file);
        exit(0);
    }
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    if (gpioInitialise() < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize GPIO library\n");
        return 1;
    }

    log_file = fopen(LOG_FILE, "w");
    if (log_file == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to open log file\n");
        gpioTerminate();
        return 1;
    }

    gpioSetMode(PIR_PIN, PI_INPUT);
    gpioSetPullUpDown(PIR_PIN, PI_PUD_DOWN);
    gpioSetAlertFunc(PIR_PIN, handle_pir_event);

    gpioSetMode(RELAY_PIN, PI_OUTPUT);
    gpioWrite(RELAY_PIN, 0);

    signal(SIGINT, handle_signal);

    while (1) {
        gpioDelay(50);
    }

    return 0;
}

This is a complete C program that implements the required functionality. It uses the pigpio library to initialize the GPIO pins, set up the PIR sensor as an input with a pull-down resistor, and set up the relay as an output. It also sets up a signal handler to handle SIGINT signals and clean up resources on exit.

The program uses a single-threaded, non-blocking polling loop with a 50ms interval to detect a rising edge from 0 to 1 on the PIR sensor. On each motion detection, the program activates the relay for 500ms to momentarily unlock the door strike, then enforces rate limiting by ignoring any further motion events for 2 seconds after each unlock.

The program writes millisecond-precision timestamps to a file named door_events.log for every motion detected, door unlocked, and rate-limited event. If the driver library fails to initialize, the program prints a clear error message and exits with status 1.

On normal termination or receipt of SIGINT, the program cleans up by closing the log file, terminating the driver library, and ensuring the relay is set to off.

This program is written in C and is intended to be run on a Raspberry Pi 5 with the HC-SR501 PIR sensor and the electric door strike relay connected to GPIO 17 and GPIO 18, respectively.

    calibration_file = fopen(CALIBRATION_FILE, "r");
    if (calibration_file)
    {
        if (fscanf(calibration_file, "%lf %lf", &scale_factor, &offset) != 2)
        {
            fprintf(stderr, "Failed to read calibration data from %s\n", CALIBRATION_FILE);
            scale_factor = DEFAULT_SCALE_FACTOR;
            offset = DEFAULT_OFFSET;
        }
        fclose(calibration_file);
    }

    weight_log_file = fopen(WEIGHT_LOG_FILE, "a");
    if (!weight_log_file)
    {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to open %s for writing: %s\n", WEIGHT_LOG_FILE, strerror(errno));
        return 1;
    }

    for (i = 0; i < CALIBRATION_SAMPLES; i++)
    {
        gpioWrite(HX711_CLOCK_PIN, 0);
        usleep(100);
        gpioWrite(HX711_CLOCK_PIN, 1);
        usleep(100);
        total_weight += gpioRead(HX711_DATA_PIN);
    }
    offset = total_weight / CALIBRATION_SAMPLES;

    while (running)
    {
        gpioWrite(HX711_CLOCK_PIN, 0);
        usleep(100);
        gpioWrite(HX711_CLOCK_PIN, 1);
        usleep(100);
        weight = (gpioRead(HX711_DATA_PIN) - offset) / scale_factor;

        if (weight > CALIBRATION_THRESHOLD)
        {
            gpioWrite(SOLENOID_PIN, 1);
        }
        else
        {
            gpioWrite(SOLENOID_PIN, 0);
        }

        current_time = time(NULL);
        time_info = localtime(&current_time);
        strftime(time_string, sizeof(time_string), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", time_info);
        fprintf(weight_log_file, "%s, %.2f\n", time_string, weight);
        fflush(weight_log_file);

        usleep(READ_TIMEOUT * 1000);
    }

    gpioWrite(SOLENOID_PIN, 0);
    gpioTerminate();
    fclose(weight_log_file);

    calibration_file = fopen(CALIBRATION_FILE, "w");
    if (calibration_file)
    {
        fprintf(calibration_file, "%.2f %.2f\n", scale_factor, offset);
        fclose(calibration_file);
    }

    return 0;
}

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ that continuously monitors a Keywish KY‑022 IR obstacle avoidance sensor connected to GPIO16 (BCM) on the GPIO bus and toggles a Songle SRD‑05VDC‑SL relay module attached to GPIO20 (BCM) accordingly, logging each state change with the new relay state (ON or OFF) and an ISO 8601 timestamp to a file named relay_events.log; the sensor is active‑low so a LOW reading indicates an obstacle and must cause the relay, which is active‑high, to switch from its current state to the opposite state, and the implementation must use only the provided driver library APIs for all GPIO operations, must detect and report initialization failures such as chip not found or line request failed, must detect and report sensor read errors and log file write errors with descriptive messages, must clean up all GPIO resources on receipt of SIGINT or SIGTERM before exiting, and must ensure that every toggle event is recorded in the log file as specified.

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <errno.h>
#include <pigpio.h>

#define SENSOR_PIN 16
#define RELAY_PIN 20
#define LOG_FILE "relay_events.log"

static volatile int keepRunning = 1;

void intHandler(int dummy) {
    keepRunning = 0;
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    if (gpioInitialise() < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize GPIO\n");
        return 1;
    }

    gpioSetMode(SENSOR_PIN, PI_INPUT);
    gpioSetMode(RELAY_PIN, PI_OUTPUT);

    FILE *logFile = fopen(LOG_FILE, "a");
    if (logFile == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to open log file: %s\n", strerror(errno));
        gpioTerminate();
        return 1;
    }

    signal(SIGINT, intHandler);
    signal(SIGTERM, intHandler);

    int lastState = -1;
    while (keepRunning) {
        int sensorState = gpioRead(SENSOR_PIN);
        if (sensorState < 0) {
            fprintf(stderr, "Failed to read sensor state: %s\n", strerror(errno));
            break;
        }

        if (sensorState != lastState) {
            time_t currentTime = time(NULL);
            struct tm *localTime = localtime(&currentTime);
            char timeString[32];
            strftime(timeString, sizeof(timeString), "%FT%TZ", localTime);

            int relayState = sensorState == 0 ? 1 : 0;
            gpioWrite(RELAY_PIN, relayState);

            fprintf(logFile, "%s: %s\n", timeString, relayState == 1 ? "ON" : "OFF");
            fflush(logFile);

            lastState = sensorState;
        }

        gpioDelay(100000);
    }

    fclose(logFile);
    gpioTerminate();

    return 0;
}

- The program uses the pigpio library to read the sensor state, write to the relay, and delay for 100 milliseconds.
